import numpy as np

def basis(i, p, M, h, etype):
    '''Inputs
    i: int, the index of element
    p: array of arbitrary size 1,2, or 3, the coordinates
    M: int, the total number of the nodal dofs
    h: int, the element size
    etype: int, basis function type; When type equals to 1, 
    it returns $\omega^1(x)$, when the type equals to 2, it returns the value of function $\omega^2(x)$.
    Outputs
    v: array of size 1,2, or 3, value of basis function
    '''
    v = np.zeros_like(p)
    
    if etype == 1:
        # w_i^1(x) = (x - x_{i-1}) / h_{i-1} defined on [x_{i-1}, x_i]
        # Indices in python: node i-1 corresponds to mesh index i-1, node i corresponds to i
        if i > 0:
            x_left = i * h
            x_right = (i + 1) * h

            # Note: The formula in prompt says w_i^1 is defined on x_{i-1} <= x <= x_i
            # x_{i-1} = (i-1)*h, x_i = i*h
            mask = (p >= (i-1)*h) & (p <= i*h)
            v[mask] = (p[mask] - (i-1)*h) / h
            
    elif etype == 2:
        # w_i^2(x) = (x_{i+1} - x) / h_i defined on [x_i, x_{i+1}]
        # x_i = i*h, x_{i+1} = (i+1)*h
        mask = (p >= i*h) & (p <= (i+1)*h)
        v[mask] = ((i+1)*h - p[mask]) / h
        
    return v
